products.name: Tinkercad
products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI features: none recorded. Use: 3D design, circuits, code blocks. Who: Students, teachers. Student age: All ages; under 13 needs parent or teacher consent; teacher-linked class accounts. Privacy: kidSAFE COPPA Safe Harbor certified; Autodesk Children's Privacy Statement (April 2026). Price: Free.

reading.body:
Autodesk holds 653 granted US patents since 2001, and its five most recent, issued between July and September 2026, are all design automation.

The recent patents cover automatic frame design for buildings, generative design for subtractive manufacturing, machine learning for sketch-to-3D shape generation, surface mesh self-intersection detection, and a variable stiffness structure built from a personal pressure map. Four of the five sit squarely in the design-to-fabrication path. The building frame patent is the one that touches construction directly, and it is the newest of the set.

For AI specifically, the sketch-to-3D patent is the clearest signal: it is a machine learning method for turning a drawing into geometry, which is the step that sits between a designer's intent and anything that gets built. Generative design patents matter for the same reason. If AI compresses design time, the downstream demand for materials, fabrication, and construction does not disappear, it arrives sooner and in larger volume. That is the compute-to-buildings chain running in reverse, from software back toward physical load.

What this data does not show is revenue, headcount, or how many of the 653 patents are actually practiced. It records one product, Tinkercad, with no AI features recorded, so the patent record and the product record describe different parts of the company. The filing list is a sequence of dates and forms with no contents, so nothing here says what Autodesk told the SEC or why it filed eight times in four months.

profile_text.body:
Autodesk is a public company traded as ADSK, registered with the SEC as Autodesk, Inc. Its website presents Tinkercad as a free, easy-to-use app for 3D design, electronics, and coding.

Tinkercad is tracked as an education and research AI product. The site describes it as covering 3D design, circuits, and code blocks, aimed at students and teachers of all ages, with parent or teacher consent required for users under 13 and teacher-linked class accounts available. No AI features are recorded for it. It is free, is kidSAFE COPPA Safe Harbor certified, and is covered by the Autodesk Children's Privacy Statement dated April 2026.

The company's SEC registration is recorded under CIK 0000769397. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for Autodesk.
